content.en: A lambda is an anonymous inline function. The compiler models it as an instance of a unique unnamed class (functor) that overloads `operator()`. Introduced in C++11, extended in C++14, C++17, and C++20.
content.ro: Un lambda este o functie anonima inlinie. Compilatorul o modeleaza ca o instanta a unei clase anonime unice (functor) care suprascrie `operator()`. Introdus in C++11, extins in C++14, C++17 si C++20.

content.en:
**Lambda syntax variants:**
- `[captures] (params) -> return_type { body }` — full form
- `[captures] (params) { body }` — return type deduced
- `[captures] { body }` — no parameters

If no variables are captured, the lambda object is typically **1 byte** in size. A no-capture lambda can be implicitly converted to a plain function pointer.
content.ro:
**Variante de sintaxa lambda:**
- `[captures] (params) -> return_type { body }` — forma completa
- `[captures] (params) { body }` — tip returnat dedus
- `[captures] { body }` — fara parametri

Daca nu sunt capturate variabile, obiectul lambda are de obicei **1 byte**. Un lambda fara capturi poate fi convertit implicit la un pointer de functie simplu.

content.en:
The capture clause defines which local variables are accessible inside the lambda body:

- `[]` — captures nothing
- `[a, b]` — capture `a` and `b` by value (copy made at lambda definition)
- `[&a, &b]` — capture `a` and `b` by reference
- `[this]` — capture the current object pointer
- `[&]` — capture all used local variables by reference
- `[=]` — capture all used local variables by value
- `[=, &a]` — all by value except `a` by reference
- `[&, a]` — all by reference except `a` by value
content.ro:
Clauza de captura defineste ce variabile locale sunt accesibile in corpul lambda:

- `[]` — nu captureaza nimic
- `[a, b]` — captureaza `a` si `b` prin valoare (copie facuta la definirea lambda)
- `[&a, &b]` — captureaza `a` si `b` prin referinta
- `[this]` — captureaza pointerul obiectului curent
- `[&]` — captureaza toate variabilele locale folosite prin referinta
- `[=]` — captureaza toate variabilele locale folosite prin valoare
- `[=, &a]` — toate prin valoare exceptand `a` prin referinta
- `[&, a]` — toate prin referinta exceptand `a` prin valoare

content.en: **Dangling reference trap:** Capturing a local variable by reference (`&`) and executing the lambda after the variable goes out of scope causes **undefined behavior**. The lambda may silently corrupt a different variable that occupies the same stack location.
content.ro: **Capcana referintei agatate:** Capturarea unei variabile locale prin referinta (`&`) si executarea lambda-ului dupa ce variabila iese din domeniu cauzeaza **comportament nedefinit**. Lambda-ul poate corupe silentios o alta variabila care ocupa aceeasi locatie pe stiva.

content.en:
The compiler translates a lambda into an anonymous struct with `operator() const`. Captured variables become **data members** of this struct. Understanding this model clarifies why:
- Captured-by-value lambdas cannot modify their captures by default (`operator()` is `const`)
- No-capture lambdas convert to function pointers (no `this` needed)
- Each distinct lambda has a **unique type** — even if they look identical
content.ro:
Compilatorul traduce un lambda intr-un struct anonim cu `operator() const`. Variabilele capturate devin **membri de date** ai acestui struct. Intelegerea acestui model clarifica de ce:
- Lambdas capturate prin valoare nu pot modifica capturile implicit (`operator()` este `const`)
- Lambdas fara capturi se convertesc la pointeri de functie (nu este nevoie de `this`)
- Fiecare lambda distinct are un **tip unic** — chiar daca arata identic

content.en:
- **`mutable`**: Removes the `const` qualifier from the generated `operator()`, allowing modification of by-value captured variables inside the lambda body.
- **Initialized capture** (C++14): Allows defining and initializing new variables in the capture block, even renaming captures: `[counter = 0]() mutable { return counter++; }`
content.ro:
- **`mutable`**: Elimina calificatorul `const` din `operator()` generat, permitand modificarea variabilelor capturate prin valoare in corpul lambda.
- **Captura initializata** (C++14): Permite definirea si initializarea de noi variabile in blocul de captura, chiar si redenumirea capturilor: `[counter = 0]() mutable { return counter++; }`

content.en:
Lambdas are the idiomatic way to supply predicates and operations to STL algorithms like `std::for_each`, `std::sort`, `std::count_if`, `std::remove_if`.

`std::function<ReturnType(Args...)>` is a type-erased wrapper that can store any callable (lambdas, function pointers, functors). It is more flexible but slower than direct function pointers due to type erasure overhead.
content.ro:
Lambdas reprezinta modul idiom de a furniza predicate si operatii algoritmilor STL ca `std::for_each`, `std::sort`, `std::count_if`, `std::remove_if`.

`std::function<TipReturnat(Args...)>` este un wrapper cu stergere de tip care poate stoca orice apelabil (lambdas, pointeri de functii, functori). Este mai flexibil dar mai lent decat pointerii de functii directi din cauza overhead-ului stergerii de tip.

content.en:
- **C++14 Generic Lambda**: `auto` parameters — acts like a template: `auto f = [](auto x, auto y) { return x + y; };`
- **C++20 Template Lambda**: Explicit template parameter for stricter constraints: `auto f = []<typename T>(T v1, T v2) { return v1 + v2; };`
- **C++17 `constexpr` Lambda**: Allows compile-time evaluation: `constexpr auto f = [](int a, int b) { return a + b; };`
- **C++17 `[*this]` Capture**: Captures a copy of `*this` (safe for async — original object may be destroyed).
content.ro:
- **Lambda Generic C++14**: Parametri `auto` — actioneaza ca un sablon: `auto f = [](auto x, auto y) { return x + y; };`
- **Lambda Template C++20**: Parametru de sablon explicit pentru constrangeri mai stricte: `auto f = []<typename T>(T v1, T v2) { return v1 + v2; };`
- **Lambda `constexpr` C++17**: Permite evaluarea la compilare: `constexpr auto f = [](int a, int b) { return a + b; };`
- **Captura `[*this]` C++17**: Captureaza o copie a `*this` (sigur pentru async — obiectul original poate fi distrus).

question.en: Why can a lambda that captures nothing be converted to a plain function pointer?
question.ro: De ce poate un lambda fara capturi sa fie convertit la un pointer de functie simplu?

text.en: Because no captured variables means the functor struct has no data members, so it behaves identically to a free function
text.ro: Pentru ca fara variabile capturate structul functor nu are membri de date, deci se comporta identic cu o functie libera

explanation.en: Without captures, the lambda's operator() needs no this pointer. The compiler can provide an implicit conversion to a function pointer.
explanation.ro: Fara capturi, operator() al lambda-ului nu are nevoie de pointerul this. Compilatorul poate furniza o conversie implicita la un pointer de functie.

text.en: Because it has no return type
text.ro: Pentru ca nu are tip de returnare

explanation.en: Return type is unrelated. A lambda can have any return type and still convert to a function pointer if it has no captures.
explanation.ro: Tipul de returnare nu are legatura. Un lambda poate avea orice tip de returnare si tot se poate converti la pointer de functie daca nu are capturi.

text.en: All lambdas can be converted to function pointers
text.ro: Toate lambdas pot fi convertite la pointeri de functii

explanation.en: Only no-capture lambdas can be implicitly converted. A lambda with captures stores data members and cannot be represented as a plain function pointer.
explanation.ro: Doar lambdas fara capturi pot fi convertite implicit. Un lambda cu capturi stocheaza membri de date si nu poate fi reprezentat ca un pointer de functie simplu.

text.en: Because function pointers are deprecated in modern C++
text.ro: Pentru ca pointerii de functii sunt deprecati in C++ modern

explanation.en: Function pointers are not deprecated. They are still widely used as callback arguments in C APIs.
explanation.ro: Pointerii de functii nu sunt deprecati. Sunt inca larg folositi ca argumente callback in API-urile C.

question.en: What does the `mutable` keyword do when applied to a lambda?
question.ro: Ce face cuvantul cheie `mutable` cand este aplicat unui lambda?

text.en: Allows the lambda to modify captured-by-reference variables
text.ro: Permite lambda-ului sa modifice variabilele capturate prin referinta

explanation.en: Captured-by-reference variables can always be modified — they are already aliases to the originals. mutable affects by-value captures.
explanation.ro: Variabilele capturate prin referinta pot fi intotdeauna modificate — sunt deja aliasuri ale originalelor. mutable afecteaza capturile prin valoare.

text.en: Removes the const qualifier from the generated operator(), allowing modification of by-value captured copies
text.ro: Elimina calificatorul const din operator() generat, permitand modificarea copiilor capturate prin valoare

explanation.en: By default, the lambda's operator() is const, preventing modification of by-value captures. mutable removes this restriction.
explanation.ro: In mod implicit, operator() al lambda-ului este const, prevenind modificarea capturilor prin valoare. mutable elimina aceasta restrictie.

explanation.en: mutable has nothing to do with thread safety. It only affects const-ness of the generated operator().
explanation.ro: mutable nu are nimic de-a face cu siguranta thread-urilor. Afecteaza doar const-itatea lui operator() generat.

text.en: Allows the lambda to be called multiple times
text.ro: Permite lambda-ului sa fie apelat de mai multe ori

explanation.en: Lambdas can always be called multiple times regardless of mutable.
explanation.ro: Lambdas pot fi intotdeauna apelate de mai multe ori indiferent de mutable.

question.en: You have `auto f = [&x]() { return x++; };` where `x` is a local variable. The lambda is returned from the function and called later. What happens?
question.ro: Ai `auto f = [&x]() { return x++; };` unde `x` este o variabila locala. Lambda-ul este returnat din functie si apelat mai tarziu. Ce se intampla?

text.en: It works correctly — the lambda keeps the variable alive
text.ro: Functioneaza corect — lambda-ul mentine variabila in viata

explanation.en: Lambdas do NOT extend the lifetime of captured references. The variable is destroyed when the function returns.
explanation.ro: Lambdas NU extind durata de viata a referintelor capturate. Variabila este distrusa cand functia returneaza.

text.en: Compile error — you cannot return a lambda that captures by reference
text.ro: Eroare de compilare — nu puteti returna un lambda care captureaza prin referinta

explanation.en: The compiler does NOT detect this as an error. It is a runtime undefined behavior trap.
explanation.ro: Compilatorul NU detecteaza aceasta ca o eroare. Este o capcana cu comportament nedefinit la runtime.

text.en: Undefined behavior — the lambda holds a dangling reference to the destroyed variable
text.ro: Comportament nedefinit — lambda-ul detine o referinta agata la variabila distrusa

explanation.en: The stack frame is gone after the function returns. Accessing x through the captured reference is undefined behavior.
explanation.ro: Cadrul de stiva dispare dupa ce functia returneaza. Accesarea lui x prin referinta capturata este comportament nedefinit.

text.en: The lambda makes a copy of x when returned
text.ro: Lambda-ul face o copie a lui x cand este returnat

explanation.en: Capture by reference stores a reference (address), not a copy. To get a copy, use [x] or [x = x] (initialized capture).
explanation.ro: Captura prin referinta stocheaza o referinta (adresa), nu o copie. Pentru a obtine o copie, folositi [x] sau [x = x] (captura initializata).
